root.label: Knowledge Repository
root.summary: A comprehensive collection of technical documentation covering audio engineering, behavioral simulation, team enablement, and evolutionary biology.

lg_root.label: Landscape Granulator
lg_root.summary: An acoustic machine designed as a site of geological acoustic events that fractures signals into microscopic artifacts and rearranges them into tectonic swells or decaying spaces.

lg_arch.label: Landscape Granulator Architecture
lg_arch.summary: The underlying system built around an auto-chopping buffer and a multi-stage diffusion network.

lg_arch_fact_1.label: Design Purpose
lg_arch_fact_1.summary: Designed to pull structure apart and build massive sonic ruins from the fragments.

lg_controls.label: Landscape Granulator Controls
lg_controls.summary: The interface used to manipulate the granulator's sonic output.

lg_dials.label: Control Dials
lg_dials.summary: The primary parametric controls for sonic manipulation.

lg_dial_grain_size.label: Grain Size (Scope)
lg_dial_grain_size.summary: Dictates the physical dimension of sonic fragments. Low settings produce microscopic clicks; high settings create long, overlapping tectonic plates of sound.

lg_dial_grain_density.label: Grain Density (Mass)
lg_dial_grain_density.summary: Controls the population of active fragments. Low settings produce sparse events; high settings create a dense monolith of noise. Density inversely dictates grain lifespan (higher density equals shorter individual lives).

lg_dial_grain_arp.label: Grain Arp (Concurrence)
lg_dial_grain_arp.summary: Forces grains into pitched intervals. Zero results in pure texture; higher settings create chordal structures, arpeggios, or microtonal sequences based on Alignment switch.

lg_dial_randomness.label: Randomness (Erosion)
lg_dial_randomness.summary: Introduces entropic jitter. Effects include unpredictable playhead origin, wildly varying grain lifespans, and destabilized looper sequence logic.

lg_dial_verb_feedback.label: Verb Mix / Master Feedback (Space)
lg_dial_verb_feedback.summary: Controls depth and intensity of the multi-tap diffusion tank. Pushing past 12 o'clock feeds delayed signals back into themselves, pushing internal filters toward screaming self-oscillation.

lg_dial_dry_wet.label: Dry / Wet (Surface)
lg_dial_dry_wet.summary: Balances uncorrupted input signal against the processed ruin.

lg_ext_control.label: External Control (EXP)
lg_ext_control.summary: Expression pedal input that simultaneously shifts Grain Size, Grain Arp, and Master Feedback.

lg_switches.label: Control Switches
lg_switches.summary: Three-position switches for Topography, Pulse, and Alignment.

lg_sw_filter.label: Filter (Topography)
lg_sw_filter.summary: HPF (Jagged/Brittle), BPF (Hollowed/Vocal), LPF (Subterranean/Warm). Driven by 16 internal LFOs.

lg_sw_chop.label: Chop (Pulse)
lg_sw_chop.summary: Determines how the auto-sampler dices phrases: 1/4 Notes (Slow/Tectonic), 1/8 Notes (Steady), 1/16 Notes (Frantic/Mechanical).

lg_sw_arp.label: Arp Mode (Alignment)
lg_sw_arp.summary: Fifths (Open/Resonant), Chromatic (Densely packed staircase), Custom (Unpredictable microtonal shifting).

lg_footswitches.label: Footswitches
lg_footswitches.summary: Hands-free control for bypass and looping operations.

lg_fs_bypass.label: Bypass (SW1)
lg_fs_bypass.summary: Engages or bypasses the entire architecture.

lg_fs_looper.label: Alt / Looper (SW2)
lg_fs_looper.summary: Complex state machine: Short tap on empty buffer starts recording; short tap on recording closes loop for playback; short tap on playing overdub; long press erases timeline.

lg_led_effect.label: Effect LED (LED1)
lg_led_effect.summary: Solid when the effect is active.

lg_led_tempo.label: Tempo & Record LED (LED2)
lg_led_tempo.summary: Flashing indicates mechanical pulse; solid indicates active recording or overdubbing.

lg_signal_path.label: Signal Path
lg_signal_path.summary: The linear sequence of processing stages.

lg_sp_2.label: Auto-Chop Sampler
lg_sp_2.summary: Anchors phrases, locks pulse, and creates foundational loop.

lg_sp_3.label: Granulator
lg_sp_3.summary: Shatters signal into grains; playback and pitch randomized by entropy settings.

lg_sp_4.label: VCA / Filter Array
lg_sp_4.summary: Grains swept through 8 panning filters driven by 16 hidden LFOs.

lg_sp_5.label: Multi-Tap Pre-Delay
lg_sp_5.summary: Filtered ruins bounced across 6 delay lines (249ms to 747ms) to widen space.

lg_sp_6.label: Diffusion Tank
lg_sp_6.summary: Echoes wash through un-synced allpass diffusers into a dense atmosphere.

lg_sp_7.label: Stereo Output Stage
lg_sp_7.summary: Hard-panned stereo field merged with uncorrupted input.

lg_settings.label: Suggested Patch Settings
lg_settings.summary: Specific knob configurations for desired sonic outcomes.

lg_patch_glacial.label: The Glacial
lg_patch_glacial.summary: Massive, slow-moving tectonic pad. LPF, Quarter notes, Fifths.

lg_patch_unstable.label: The Unstable
lg_patch_unstable.summary: Stuttering mechanical breakdown for drums/synths. HPF, Sixteenth notes, Custom Arp.

lg_patch_ascendant.label: The Ascendant
lg_patch_ascendant.summary: Cascading pitched-up shimmer. BPF, Eighth notes, Chromatic Arp.

lg_patch_geothermal.label: The Geothermal
lg_patch_geothermal.summary: Saturated sub-harmonics on the edge of chaos. LPF, Quarter notes, Custom Arp.

lg_patch_scratched.label: The Scratched
lg_patch_scratched.summary: Brittle icy textures for ambient guitar. HPF, Eighth notes, Fifths.

lg_patch_memory.label: The Memory
lg_patch_memory.summary: Mutated, degraded artifacts via looper. BPF, Sixteenth notes, Chromatic Arp.

boid_root.label: Boids / Distributed Behavioral Model
boid_root.summary: A simulation approach to aggregate motion (flocking) based on the interaction of independent actors following simple local behaviors.

boid_fundamentals.label: Boid Fundamentals
boid_fundamentals.summary: The conceptual basis of the boid model relative to other systems.

boid_particle_systems.label: Relation to Particle Systems
boid_particle_systems.summary: Boids are a generalization of particle systems. Unlike dots, boids have full local coordinate systems, orientation, and strong interaction between particles.

boid_actor_model.label: The Actor Model
boid_actor_model.summary: A computational abstraction combining process, procedure, and state. Boids are implemented as actors (virtual computers) that communicate via message passing.

boid_behavioral_animation.label: Behavioral Animation
boid_behavioral_animation.summary: Modeling the behavior of a character rather than scripting paths. The animator becomes a 'meta-animator' or theatrical director designing behavior.

boid_flight.label: Geometric Flight
boid_flight.summary: The physical simulation of movement along a 3D curve.

boid_flight_mechanics.label: Flight Mechanics
boid_flight_mechanics.summary: Incremental translations along the local Z axis (forward), intermixed with pitch (X-axis rotation) and yaw (Y-axis rotation).

boid_banking.label: Banking
boid_banking.summary: Rotation about the local Z axis. Aligns the local Y axis with the total acceleration vector (lateral and gravitational). Coordinated turns match viewer expectations of flight.

boid_momentum.label: Conservation of Momentum
boid_momentum.summary: Includes viscous speed damping (max speed limit) and maximum acceleration truncation to ensure smooth heading and speed changes.

boid_behaviors.label: Flocking Behaviors
boid_behaviors.summary: The three primary rules that create aggregate motion, listed in order of precedence.

boid_beh_collision.label: Collision Avoidance
boid_beh_collision.summary: The highest priority rule: steer away from imminent impact based on relative position of flockmates.

boid_beh_velocity.label: Velocity Matching
boid_beh_velocity.summary: The predictive version of collision avoidance: attempt to match the heading and speed of nearby flockmates to maintain invariant separation.

boid_beh_centering.label: Flock Centering
boid_beh_centering.summary: The urge to move toward the centroid of nearby flockmates. This allow flocks to bifurcate around obstacles.

boid_beh_arbitration.label: Behavioral Arbitration
boid_beh_arbitration.summary: Requests are processed via prioritized acceleration allocation. Acceleration is parceled out to satisfy high-priority needs first; if the maximum acceleration is reached, lower-priority behaviors are ignored.

boid_perception.label: Simulated Perception
boid_perception.summary: How boids access environmental data to mimic biological limitations.

boid_perc_locality.label: Localized Perception
boid_perc_locality.summary: Neighborhoods are defined as spherical zones of sensitivity centered at the boid's origin. Sensitivity is an inverse exponential of distance.

boid_perc_weighting.label: Distance Weighting
boid_perc_weighting.summary: The model uses an inverse square of the distance (gravity-like) to determine influence, correlating with biological findings (visual angle and pressure waves).

boid_perc_obstacles.label: Obstacle Avoidance
boid_perc_obstacles.summary: Steer-to-avoid: The boid finds the silhouette edge of an obstacle on its Z-axis and aims for a point one body length beyond that edge.

boid_tech_complexity.label: Algorithmic Complexity
boid_tech_complexity.summary: The naive implementation is O(N^2). To achieve constant time, spatial partitioning (bins) or incremental collision detection is required.

boid_tech_env.label: Computing Environment
boid_tech_env.summary: Written in Symbolics Common Lisp using Flavors (OO extensions), running on a Symbolics 3600 Lisp Machine with S-Geometry and S-Dynamics.

astec_root.label: ASTEC™ Engagement Cycle™
astec_root.summary: An orientation for thoughtful team enablement moving through Awareness, Sense, Think, and Enable, surrounded by Celebration.

astec_awareness.label: Awareness
astec_awareness.summary: Disciplined observation without intervention. Focused on noticing patterns, energy, and timing without trying to influence or explain.

astec_aw_stance.label: Awareness Stance
astec_aw_stance.summary: Present, open, and non-reactive. Notice influence without reacting to it.

astec_aw_discipline.label: Awareness Discipline
astec_aw_discipline.summary: Avoid early exits such as explaining, reframing, offering reassurance, or naming causes before patterns stabilize.

astec_sense.label: Sense
astec_sense.summary: Meaning-making without blame. Hypothesizing on the drivers of observed system behavior.

astec_se_stance.label: Sense Stance
astec_se_stance.summary: Sense-making, not judgment. Form working hypotheses, not conclusions.

astec_se_method.label: Sense-making Method
astec_se_method.summary: Integrate across perspectives, hold contradictions, and notice where stories diverge without privileging the loudest narrative.

astec_think.label: Think
astec_think.summary: Intentional, disciplined decision-making regarding what deserves action and what should be left alone.

astec_th_stance.label: Think Stance
astec_th_stance.summary: Intentional, thoughtful, and disciplined. Guard against 'heroics' (rescuing) and 'urgency traps'.

astec_th_restraint.label: Active Restraint
astec_th_restraint.summary: Choosing a smaller move over sweeping change or allowing discomfort to persist to protect the system's learning capacity.

astec_th_ownership.label: Ownership Constraint
astec_th_ownership.summary: Crucial question: 'Who will own this once I step back?' If the answer is 'me', the move does not belong in Enable.

astec_enable.label: Enable
astec_enable.summary: Action without control. Changing conditions so the system can respond differently.

astec_en_stance.label: Enable Stance
astec_en_stance.summary: Light-touch, non-owning. The aim is to be unnecessary later.

astec_en_conditions.label: Condition Modification
astec_en_conditions.summary: Changing decision rights, information flow, handoffs, visibility of risk, or incentives rather than directly changing behavior.

astec_en_coaching.label: Enablement Coaching
astec_en_coaching.summary: Expanding agency by building confidence or inviting new perspectives. Becomes control if it creates dependence on the TEC's judgment.

astec_celebration.label: Celebration
astec_celebration.summary: An environment, not a step. Making learning visible and reinforcing ownership without creating dependency.

astec_ce_purpose.label: Purpose of Celebration
astec_ce_purpose.summary: Notice what is different. Signals what matters (e.g., improved decision-making, clearer ownership).

astec_ce_boundary.label: Celebration Boundary
astec_ce_boundary.summary: Celebration belongs to the system, not the TEC. The TEC is a catalyst, not the source of validation.

astec_transitions.label: ASTEC Transitions
astec_transitions.summary: Interior discernment moments to shift attention between phases.

astec_tr_aw_se.label: Awareness -> Sense
astec_tr_aw_se.summary: Shift from noticing to understanding. Occurs when a pattern is persistent and worth understanding more deeply.

astec_tr_se_th.label: Sense -> Think
astec_tr_se_th.summary: Shift from understanding to possibility. Occurs when working hypotheses feel coherent and stable enough to explore.

astec_tr_th_en.label: Think -> Enable
astec_tr_th_en.summary: Shift from possibility to movement. Occurs when a well-considered action would help the system work better and continued thinking provides diminishing returns.

evo_root.label: Evolutionary Biology
evo_root.summary: The study of changes in the gene pool of a population over time, uniting all fields of biology under one theoretical umbrella.

evo_def_evo.label: Evolution
evo_def_evo.summary: A change in the gene pool of a population over time. Populations evolve, not individuals.

evo_def_gene.label: Gene
evo_def_gene.summary: A hereditary unit that can be passed on unaltered for many generations.

evo_def_pool.label: Gene Pool
evo_def_pool.summary: The set of all genes in a species or population.

evo_def_phenotype.label: Phenotype
evo_def_phenotype.summary: The morphological, physiological, biochemical, and behavioral properties exhibited by an organism, determined by genes and environment.

evo_def_micro_macro.label: Microevolution vs Macroevolution
evo_def_micro_macro.summary: Microevolution involves small changes in gene frequency. Macroevolution involves larger changes, such as the formation of new species.

evo_variation.label: Genetic Variation
evo_variation.summary: The prerequisite for evolution, consisting of allelic diversity and non-random associations.

evo_var_allele.label: Allele
evo_var_allele.summary: An alternate version of a gene created by mutation.

evo_var_locus.label: Locus
evo_var_locus.summary: The specific location of a gene on a chromosome.

evo_var_hom_het.label: Homozygous vs Heterozygous
evo_var_hom_het.summary: Homozygous: an individual with two identical alleles at a locus. Heterozygous: an individual with two different alleles at a locus.

evo_var_linkage.label: Linkage Disequilibrium
evo_var_linkage.summary: The non-random association between alleles of two different genes. Calculated as D = f(A1B1)*f(A2B2) - f(A1B2)*f(A2B1).

evo_mechanisms.label: Mechanisms of Evolution
evo_mechanisms.summary: Processes that either increase or decrease genetic variation.

evo_mech_decrease.label: Variation-Decreasing Mechanisms
evo_mech_decrease.summary: Processes that remove genetic diversity from the pool.

evo_sel_natural.label: Natural Selection
evo_sel_natural.summary: Differential reproductive success of pre-existing genetic variants. It is the only mechanism of adaptive evolution.

evo_sel_balancing.label: Balancing Selection
evo_sel_balancing.summary: Selection favoring heterozygotes (e.g., sickle-cell allele maintenance in malaria-prone regions).

evo_sel_sexual.label: Sexual Selection
evo_sel_sexual.summary: Natural selection operating on mating success. Includes 'Good Genes' (display as viability signal) and 'Runaway Selection' (positive feedback loop of preference and trait).

evo_drift.label: Genetic Drift
evo_drift.summary: Random change in allele frequencies due to binomial sampling error. Pronounced in small populations; includes the Founder Effect.

evo_mech_increase.label: Variation-Increasing Mechanisms
evo_mech_increase.summary: Processes that introduce new genetic material or combinations.

evo_inc_mutation.label: Mutation
evo_inc_mutation.summary: Errors in DNA copying. Can be point mutations, deletions, insertions, inversions, or duplications. Most are neutral or deleterious; few are beneficial.

evo_inc_recombination.label: Recombination
evo_inc_recombination.summary: Gene shuffling during meiosis where homologous chromosomes break and rejoin, creating new combinations of alleles.

evo_inc_gene_flow.label: Gene Flow
evo_inc_gene_flow.summary: Introduction of alleles via migration or horizontal transfer (e.g., P elements in Drosophila via parasitic mites).

evo_lineage.label: Evolution within a Lineage
evo_lineage.summary: The macro-scale patterns of common descent and adaptation.

evo_lin_inclusive_fit.label: Inclusive Fitness
evo_lin_inclusive_fit.summary: The sum of direct fitness (own offspring) and indirect fitness (alleles passed via relatives). Explains altruistic behavior in kin.

evo_lin_landscape.label: Adaptive Landscape
evo_lin_landscape.summary: The model where populations move toward local optima. Transition to global optima may be blocked by less adaptive states.

evo_lin_exaptation.label: Adaptation vs Exaptation
evo_lin_exaptation.summary: Adaptation: a trait evolved for its current utility. Exaptation: a trait evolved for one purpose but later used for another (e.g., penguin wings).

evo_lin_common_descent.label: Common Descent
evo_lin_common_descent.summary: The principle that all species descended from a common ancestor. Evolution is a branching tree, not a ladder.

evolutionary_biology.label: Evolutionary Biology
evolutionary_biology.summary: The study of biological populations, common ancestry, and the processes of modification with descent.

macroevolution_evidence.label: Evidence for Macroevolution
macroevolution_evidence.summary: Fields of study providing empirical evidence for common ancestry and modification with descent.

biochemical_genetic_evidence.label: Biochemical and Genetic Evidence
biochemical_genetic_evidence.summary: Evidence derived from gene sequences and molecular similarity between species.

fact_gene_similarity.label: Gene Sequence Similarity
fact_gene_similarity.summary: Closely related species have similar gene sequences; redundancy in nucleotides and positions of introns/pseudogenes are inherited from common ancestors. [TalkOrigins]

fact_nucleotide_divergence.label: Divergence Time and Rates
fact_nucleotide_divergence.summary: Sequence similarity is a function of divergence time. Silent sites evolve faster (4.61 per 10^9 years) than replacement sites (0.85 per 10^9 years). [TalkOrigins]

molecular_genetics.label: Molecular Genetics
molecular_genetics.summary: The technical basis of genetic material, transcription, and translation.

fact_dna_composition.label: DNA Composition
fact_dna_composition.summary: DNA consists of nucleotides: Adenine (A), Guanine (G), Cytosine (C), and Thymine (T). [TalkOrigins]

fact_rna_composition.label: RNA Composition
fact_rna_composition.summary: Similar to DNA but uses Uracil (U) instead of Thymine (T). [TalkOrigins]

protein_synthesis.label: Protein Synthesis
protein_synthesis.summary: The process of turning genetic code into functional proteins.

fact_codon_definition.label: Codons
fact_codon_definition.summary: Blocks of three nucleotides designating an amino acid. There are 64 codons for 20 amino acids, leading to redundancy. [TalkOrigins]

fact_transcription_translation.label: Transcription and Translation
fact_transcription_translation.summary: Genes are transcribed into messenger RNA (mRNA), which is translated by ribosomes into amino acid strings (proteins). [TalkOrigins]

genomic_structures.label: Genomic Structures
genomic_structures.summary: Non-coding and specialized regions of the genome.

fact_pseudogenes.label: Pseudogenes
fact_pseudogenes.summary: Inactivated copies of working genes that evolve faster because mutations do not affect organism fitness. [TalkOrigins]

fact_introns_exons.label: Introns and Exons
fact_introns_exons.summary: Exons are coding portions; Introns are non-coding sequences spliced out of mRNA before translation. [TalkOrigins]

fact_silent_replacement_sites.label: Silent vs. Replacement Sites
fact_silent_replacement_sites.summary: Silent sites are nucleotide positions that can change without altering the protein sequence; replacement sites cause amino acid substitution. [TalkOrigins]

speciation_extinction.label: Speciation and Extinction
speciation_extinction.summary: Processes that increase and decrease biological diversity.

speciation_modes.label: Modes of Speciation
speciation_modes.summary: The geographical and reproductive mechanisms of species divergence.

fact_allopatric_speciation.label: Allopatric Speciation
fact_allopatric_speciation.summary: Occurs when populations are split by geographical isolation, leading to independent gene pool changes. [TalkOrigins]

fact_sympatric_speciation.label: Sympatric Speciation
fact_sympatric_speciation.summary: Reproductive isolation occurs without geographical isolation (e.g., apple maggot fly Rhagolettis pomenella switching host plants). [TalkOrigins]

extinction_types.label: Types of Extinction
extinction_types.summary: The removal of species from the biosphere.

fact_ordinary_extinction.label: Ordinary Extinction
fact_ordinary_extinction.summary: Caused by competitive exclusion, habitat loss, or prey defense. [TalkOrigins]

fact_mass_extinction.label: Mass Extinction
fact_mass_extinction.summary: Catastrophic events wiping out many groups, followed by radiation. Examples: Permian (250mya) and K/T Boundary (65mya). [TalkOrigins]

punctuated_equilibrium.label: Punctuated Equilibrium
punctuated_equilibrium.summary: Theory by Eldredge and Gould suggesting evolution consists of long stasis interrupted by rapid change during speciation. [TalkOrigins]

fact_species_selection.label: Species Selection
fact_species_selection.summary: The hypothesis that selection acts upon species as units, analogous to natural selection acting on alleles. [TalkOrigins]

history_of_life.label: History of Life
history_of_life.summary: Chronological development of life on Earth.

rna_world.label: RNA World Hypothesis
rna_world.summary: The theory that the first replicating molecules were RNA, which acted as both genetic material and catalysts (polymerases). [TalkOrigins]

fact_prokaryotes.label: Prokaryotes
fact_prokaryotes.summary: Ordinary bacteria; earliest fossils (stromatolites) date to 3.5 billion years ago. [TalkOrigins]

fact_archaebacteria.label: Archaebacteria
fact_archaebacteria.summary: Thermophilic, methanogenic, and halophilic bacteria closely related to eukaryotes. [TalkOrigins]

fact_eukaryotes.label: Eukaryotes
fact_eukaryotes.summary: Organisms with nucleus and organelles, including protists, fungi, plants, and animals. [TalkOrigins]

fact_psi_anoxygenic.label: Photosystem I (PSI)
fact_psi_anoxygenic.summary: Early system converting CO2 and H2S to glucose, releasing sulfur. [TalkOrigins]

fact_psii_oxygenic.label: Photosystem II (PSII)
fact_psii_oxygenic.summary: Later system converting CO2 and H2O to glucose, releasing oxygen; led to the 'Oxygen Holocaust'. [TalkOrigins]

endosymbiosis.label: Endosymbiotic Theory
endosymbiosis.summary: Theory championed by Lynn Margulis that mitochondria and chloroplasts originated as engulfed free-living bacteria. [TalkOrigins]

complex_adaptive_systems.label: Complex Adaptive Systems (CAS)
complex_adaptive_systems.summary: Systems with independent components interacting locally to produce emergent global behavior.

cas_definition.label: CAS Definition
cas_definition.summary: A system of independent simple components interacting nonlinearly, exhibiting self-organization without central control, yielding emergent behavior. [Abbott/Hadžikadić]

fact_agents_definition.label: Agents
fact_agents_definition.summary: The smallest unit of organization in a CAS, governed by simple stimulus-response rules. [Abbott/Hadžikadić]

fact_aggregation.label: Aggregation
fact_aggregation.summary: The process where agents combine to produce emergent behaviors, forming 'aggregate agents' which further group into larger CAS. [Abbott/Hadžikadić]

systems_thinking.label: Systems Thinking
systems_thinking.summary: Approach studying interdependent component systems (system of systems) and global state changes. [Abbott/Hadžikadić]

fact_goal_seeking_behavior.label: Goal-Seeking Behavior
fact_goal_seeking_behavior.summary: Component systems producing a single fixed response (uni-minded) in a single environment. [Abbott/Hadžikadić]

fact_purposeful_behavior.label: Purposeful Behavior
fact_purposeful_behavior.summary: Component systems producing multiple varied responses to multiple stimuli (multi-minded), providing high potential for novel emergence. [Abbott/Hadžikadić]

agent_based_modeling.label: Agent-Based Modeling (ABM)
agent_based_modeling.summary: Computational representation of agents and their interactions with the environment to explore emergent behavior. [Abbott/Hadžikadić]

fact_internal_model.label: Internal Model
fact_internal_model.summary: The mechanism used by an agent to issue a response and 'learn' new rules through interaction. [Abbott/Hadžikadić]

fact_abm_characteristics.label: ABM Characteristics
fact_abm_characteristics.summary: Sensitive to initial conditions; used when systems are NP-Hard/NP-Complete and analytical equations are intractable. [Abbott/Hadžikadić]

systems_dynamics.label: Systems Dynamics (SD)
systems_dynamics.summary: Modeling method using state variables and systems of difference equations. [Abbott/Hadžikadić]

causal_loop_diagramming.label: Causal Loop Diagramming (CLD)
causal_loop_diagramming.summary: Visual description of system interactions using reinforcing (positive) and balancing (negative) feedback loops. [Abbott/Hadžikadić]

sugarscape_simulation.label: Sugarscape Simulation
sugarscape_simulation.summary: A social simulation model following rules for agents in a resource grid. [Sugarscape]

sugarscape_rules.label: Sugarscape Rules
sugarscape_rules.summary: The behavioral logic of the simulation.

fact_movement_rule.label: Movement Rule (M)
fact_movement_rule.summary: Agents look in 4 directions up to 'vision' distance and move to the vacant patch with highest sugar. [Sugarscape]

fact_reproduction_rule.label: Reproduction Rule (S)
fact_reproduction_rule.summary: Fertile agents of opposite sex adjacent to an empty patch deplete sugar to create a new agent. [Sugarscape]

fact_trading_rule.label: Trading Rule (T)
fact_trading_rule.summary: Agents trade resources based on Marginal Rate of Substitution (MRS) to increase welfare. [Sugarscape]

fact_lending_rule.label: Lending Rule (L)
fact_lending_rule.summary: Wealthy agents lend sugar to fertile borrowers for reproduction at a specific interest rate. [Sugarscape]

sugarscape_emergence.label: Emergent Phenomena in Sugarscape
sugarscape_emergence.summary: Complex outcomes resulting from simple local rules.

fact_terracing.label: Terracing
fact_terracing.summary: Agents gathering on borders of sugar regions when growback rate is high. [Sugarscape]

fact_migration_waves.label: Migration Waves
fact_migration_waves.summary: Populations propagating diagonally across the grid, a behavior not present in individual agents. [Sugarscape]

fact_social_hierarchy.label: Social Hierarchy
fact_social_hierarchy.summary: Emergence of distinct classes: lenders (top), lender/borrowers, and borrowers (bottom). [Sugarscape]

marl_llm_collaboration.label: MARL for LLM Collaboration
marl_llm_collaboration.summary: Using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning to optimize coordination between Large Language Models.

dec_pomdp_formalism.label: Dec-POMDP Formalism
dec_pomdp_formalism.summary: Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process used to model cooperative LLM collaboration. [Liu et al.]

fact_dec_pomdp_tuple.label: Dec-POMDP Tuple
fact_dec_pomdp_tuple.summary: Defined by <I, S, {Oi}, {Ai}, R, T, H>: I(agents), S(global state), Oi(observation space), Ai(action space), R(joint reward), T(transition function), H(horizon). [Liu et al.]

posg_comparison.label: POSG Comparison
posg_comparison.summary: Comparison between Dec-POMDP and Partially Observable Stochastic Games.

fact_posg_nash_equilibrium.label: POSG Nash Equilibrium
fact_posg_nash_equilibrium.summary: In POSG, agents maximize individual returns; a Nash Equilibrium (NE) occurs when no agent can unilaterally improve their return. [Liu et al.]

fact_posg_suboptimality.label: POSG Suboptimality
fact_posg_suboptimality.summary: Nash Equilibria in POSGs may lead to collective utilities that are suboptimal compared to the joint optimum. [Liu et al.]

magrpo_algorithm.label: MAGRPO Algorithm
magrpo_algorithm.summary: Multi-Agent Group Relative Policy Optimization for joint training of LLMs with decentralized execution. [Liu et al.]

fact_magrpo_mechanism.label: MAGRPO Mechanism
fact_magrpo_mechanism.summary: Combines centralized group-relative advantages for optimization with decentralized execution for efficiency. [Liu et al.]

fact_group_relative_advantage.label: Group Relative Advantage
fact_group_relative_advantage.summary: Estimates the return of a history by averaging over a group of Monte Carlo samples to stabilize training without a large value model. [Liu et al.]

writing_collaboration.label: Writing Collaboration
writing_collaboration.summary: Tasks involving TLDR summarization and arXiv abstract expansion. [Liu et al.]

fact_writing_metrics.label: Writing Evaluation Metrics
fact_writing_metrics.summary: Quality measured by Structure (length ratios), Style Consistency (Jaccard similarity), and Logical Coherence (transition word counts). [Liu et al.]

coding_collaboration.label: Coding Collaboration
coding_collaboration.summary: Collaborative generation of Python functions using a main generator and a helper agent. [Liu et al.]

fact_human_eval_che.label: HumanEval and CoopHumanEval
fact_human_eval_che.summary: CHE is a dataset constructed from HE specifically for problems with cooperative potential. [Liu et al.]

fact_coding_reward_levels.label: Coding Reward Hierarchy
fact_coding_reward_levels.summary: Rewards are level-based: Structural Integrity -> Syntactic Correctness -> Test Pass Rate -> Cooperation Quality Bonus. [Liu et al.]

llm_cooperation.label: Multi-Agent LLM Cooperation (MAGRPO)
llm_cooperation.summary: A framework for training LLMs to collaborate using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) and GRPO, specifically focusing on coding and writing tasks.

magrpo_metrics.label: Evaluation Metrics (@k)
magrpo_metrics.summary: Metrics used to evaluate LLM capacity by measuring the best outcome among k generated solutions to reduce variance.

pass_at_k.label: Pass@k
pass_at_k.summary: The probability that at least one out of k generated solutions passes all test cases.

pass_at_k_fact.label: Pass@k Definition
pass_at_k_fact.summary: Calculated as 1/|D| * sum(E[max p in P 1(npass = nj)]), where 1 is the indicator function for all tests passing.

acc_at_k.label: Accuracy@k (Acc@k)
acc_at_k.summary: The highest test accuracy (passed tests / total tests) among k generated solutions, averaged across all problems.

acc_at_k_fact.label: Acc@k Definition
acc_at_k_fact.summary: Provides a fine-grained assessment compared to Pass@k by treating functional correctness as a continuous variable (npass/nj).

coop_at_k.label: Cooperation@k (Coop@k)
coop_at_k.summary: The average of the highest normalized cooperation return achieved among k runs across all problems.

coop_at_k_fact.label: Coop@k Definition
coop_at_k_fact.summary: Defined as Rcoop = H^-1 * sum(rcoop_p,t from t=0 to H-1), representing normalized return over horizon H.

cooperation_schemes.label: Emergent Cooperation Schemes
cooperation_schemes.summary: Naturally emerging interaction patterns between auxiliary and main agents under minimal constraints.

fallback_scheme.label: Fallback Scheme
fallback_scheme.summary: The main agent implements a secondary solution as a backup in case the auxiliary function causes runtime errors.

fallback_fact.label: Fallback Utility
fallback_fact.summary: Benefits smaller models prone to syntax and runtime errors by enhancing code robustness.

decorator_scheme.label: Decorator Scheme
decorator_scheme.summary: The main agent trusts the auxiliary agent's core logic and adds complementary features like edge case handling or output reformatting.

decorator_fact.label: Decorator Utility
decorator_fact.summary: Necessity depends on the auxiliary agent's completeness; can become redundant if the auxiliary agent already handles edge cases.

coordinator_scheme.label: Coordinator Scheme
coordinator_scheme.summary: The main agent divides tasks into parts (e.g., using a for-loop iterator) and assigns subtasks to the auxiliary agent.

coordinator_fact.label: Coordinator Stability
coordinator_fact.summary: Unstable because the entire solution fails if the auxiliary agent fails a single subtask.

strategy_filter_scheme.label: Strategy Filter Scheme
strategy_filter_scheme.summary: The auxiliary agent acts as a filter for specific logic branches, typically appearing within conditional blocks (if statements).

strategy_filter_fact.label: Strategy Filter Utility
strategy_filter_fact.summary: Resembles adaptive control flow in software pipelines, enhancing modularity by evaluating preconditions.

learning_modes.label: MAGRPO Learning Modes
learning_modes.summary: Different methods of training agents to improve cooperative behavior.

self_improvement_mode.label: Self-Improvement Mode
self_improvement_mode.summary: Agents interact with tasks using only previous turn prompts and responses without external feedback.

self_improvement_fact.label: Self-Improvement Outcome
self_improvement_fact.summary: Learning is primarily driven by direct task interaction; second-turn performance remains similar to first-turn.

guided_learning_mode.label: Guided-Learning Mode
guided_learning_mode.summary: Agents leverage external feedback (e.g., expert agents, static checkers like AST, sandbox tests) to refine responses.

guided_learning_fact.label: Guided-Learning Outcome
guided_learning_fact.summary: Second-turn performance exceeds first-turn and outperforms self-improvement, indicating guidance is more efficient for refinement.

reward_specifications.label: Reward Specifications
reward_specifications.summary: Hierarchical reward modeling schemes used to prioritize fundamental objectives across different tasks.

writing_rewards.label: Writing Collaboration Rewards
writing_rewards.summary: Rewards for TLDR Summarization and arXiv Expansion.

structural_wellness_writing.label: Structural Wellness (Writing)
structural_wellness_writing.summary: Assessed via paragraph length ratios and unique word ratios (excluding stopwords).

style_consistency_writing.label: Style Consistency (Writing)
style_consistency_writing.summary: Measured via Jaccard similarity of vocabulary between completions, capped at 0.03 for TLDR.

logical_coherence_writing.label: Logical Coherence (Writing)
logical_coherence_writing.summary: Evaluated by the presence and diversity of transition words across 12 categories; r = min(0.6 log(n + 1), 1).

coding_rewards.label: Coding Collaboration Rewards
coding_rewards.summary: Rewards focused on functional and structural correctness of code.

structural_integrity_coding.label: Structural Integrity
structural_integrity_coding.summary: Verifies that both auxiliary and main functions are properly defined with return statements.

syntactical_correctness_coding.label: Syntactical Correctness
syntactical_correctness_coding.summary: Verified via static analysis (Abstract Syntax Tree - AST); syntax errors lead to evaluation termination.

test_pass_rate_coding.label: Test Pass Rate
test_pass_rate_coding.summary: Percentage of unit tests passed with a 10-second timeout per test.

cooperation_quality_coding.label: Cooperation Quality
cooperation_quality_coding.summary: Bonus if main function calls aux; additional rewards for substantive logic beyond wrapping.

prompt_design.label: Prompt Design
prompt_design.summary: Specific instructional sets used to define agent roles.

auxiliary_agent_prompt.label: Auxiliary Agent Prompt
auxiliary_agent_prompt.summary: Instructs the agent to create a helper function named 'aux' that returns useful data, with strict formatting constraints (no markdown, no explanations).

main_agent_prompt.label: Main Agent Prompt
main_agent_prompt.summary: Instructs the agent to implement a specific entry point function, providing access to the 'aux()' function without redefining it.

external_agent_prompt.label: External Agent Prompt
external_agent_prompt.summary: Used for multi-turn feedback; acts as an advisor providing JSON-formatted edits for 'aux' and 'main' fields.

moa_framework.label: Mixture-of-Agents (MoA)
moa_framework.summary: A layered architecture that leverages the collective strengths of multiple LLMs through iterative refinement.

collaborativeness_phenomenon.label: Collaborativeness of LLMs
collaborativeness_phenomenon.summary: The observation that LLMs generate better responses when presented with outputs from other models, even if those models are less capable.

collaborativeness_fact.label: Collaborativeness Utility
collaborativeness_fact.summary: Enables a model to refine and synthesize higher-quality outputs by leveraging diverse perspectives from auxiliary responses.

moa_architecture.label: MoA Architecture
moa_architecture.summary: A layered structure where each layer i consists of n LLMs (Ai,1 ... Ai,n).

moa_flow_fact.label: MoA Process Flow
moa_flow_fact.summary: Layer 1 agents independently generate responses; these are concatenated and passed as input to Layer 2 agents for refinement, continuing for l layers.

moa_roles.label: MoA Roles
moa_roles.summary: Different LLMs excel in different collaborative roles within the MoA ecosystem.

proposers_role.label: Proposers
proposers_role.summary: Models that excel at generating useful reference responses providing context and diverse perspectives.

aggregators_role.label: Aggregators
aggregators_role.summary: Models proficient in synthesizing multiple responses into a single, high-quality output.

moe_analogy.label: MoA vs MoE (Mixture-of-Experts)
moe_analogy.summary: MoA extends the MoE concept from the activation level to the model level.

moe_comparison_fact.label: MoA vs MoE Difference
moe_comparison_fact.summary: Unlike MoE, which uses gating networks and internal weights, MoA operates entirely through the prompt interface and requires no fine-tuning.

agent_forest.label: Agent Forest
agent_forest.summary: A sampling-and-voting method where LLM performance scales with the number of instantiated agents.

agent_forest_phases.label: Agent Forest Phases
agent_forest_phases.summary: The two-step process to derive a final answer from multiple agent outputs.

sampling_phase.label: Sampling Phase
sampling_phase.summary: Querying the LLM M (or integrated function fM) N times to create a set of samples S = {s1, ..., sN}.

voting_phase.label: Voting Phase
voting_phase.summary: Using majority voting to select the final answer A based on cumulative similarity V(si) = sum(sim(si, sj)).

agent_forest_scaling.label: Scaling Property
agent_forest_scaling.summary: Performance generally improves as the ensemble size (N) increases, allowing smaller models to outperform larger single models.

difficulty_dimensions.label: Task Difficulty Dimensions
difficulty_dimensions.summary: Three orthogonal dimensions that influence the effectiveness of the Agent Forest method.

inherent_difficulty.label: Inherent Difficulty
inherent_difficulty.summary: The core complexity of the task; performance gains increase then decrease as difficulty rises (diminishing returns at extreme complexity).

reasoning_steps.label: Number of Reasoning Steps
reasoning_steps.summary: The length of the solution path; performance gains increase as the number of steps increases.

prior_probability.label: Prior Probability
prior_probability.summary: The probability of the correct answer among possible outcomes; absolute performance increases with prior probability.

mycelium_networks.label: Mycelium as a Network
mycelium_networks.summary: Biological study of fungal mycelia as interconnected networks of hyphae affecting ecological behavior.

hyphal_growth.label: Hyphal Tip Growth
hyphal_growth.summary: The process of expansion at the hyphal apex through polarized secretion.

spitzenkoffer_fact.label: Spitzenkörper
spitzenkoffer_fact.summary: The organizer of polarized secretion at the hyphal apex, coordinating vesicles for wall material deposition.

turgor_pressure_fact.label: Turgor Pressure
turgor_pressure_fact.summary: The driving force for tip extension, maintained by water uptake through osmosis in response to solute accumulation.

mycelium_transport.label: Resource Transport
mycelium_transport.summary: The movement of solutes and organelles across the fungal network.

cytoplasmic_streaming.label: Cytoplasmic Streaming
cytoplasmic_streaming.summary: Motor-driven transport of vesicles and organelles along microtubules and microfilaments, increasing effective transport rates for solutes.

diffusion_limit_fact.label: Diffusion Limits
diffusion_limit_fact.summary: Diffusion is sufficient for short-range local growth but insufficient for long-distance translocation in large forest-floor networks.

transport_mechanisms.label: Intracellular Transport Mechanisms
transport_mechanisms.summary: The physical processes by which solutes, organelles, and macromolecules move through the hyphal network.

diffusive_movement.label: Diffusive Movement
diffusive_movement.summary: Passive movement of molecules based on concentration gradients; highly inefficient for large molecules over long distances.

diff_fact_1.label: Diffusion Time-scales
diff_fact_1.summary: Small molecules take 20h to cross 10mm; proteins take 7 weeks to cross 10mm (Page 4).

diff_fact_2.label: Macroscopic Diffusion Constraint
diff_fact_2.summary: Transport over a 25-cm microcosm would take 1.5 years for small molecules and 100 years for proteins (Page 4).

motor_driven_transport.label: Motor-Driven Transport
motor_driven_transport.summary: Active transport using cytoskeletal tracks (microtubules and actin) to move cargo at constant velocities.

mt_motors.label: Microtubule-Based Motors
mt_motors.summary: Fast motors in fungi capable of transporting cargo over medium-length scales (mm to cm).

mt_fact_1.label: Microtubule Velocity
mt_fact_1.summary: Fungal microtubule motors operate at speeds of 1 to 4 μm s–1 (Page 4).

myosin_fact_1.label: Myosin V and XI Velocity
myosin_fact_1.summary: Myosin V in yeast transports vesicles at ~3 μm s–1; Myosin XI in characean algae reaches 100 μm s–1, though such high speeds are not observed in fungi (Page 4).

motor_energetics.label: Energetics of Motor Transport
motor_energetics.summary: Costs scale with pathway length, track assembly (microfilaments/microtubules), vesicle size, speed, and cytoplasmic viscosity (Page 4).

mass_flow.label: Growth-Induced Mass Flow
mass_flow.summary: Passive movement of solutes and organelles (vacuoles, nuclei) driven by apical cell wall expansion and subapical water uptake.

peclet_number.label: Péclet Number (Pe)
peclet_number.summary: A dimensionless ratio used to determine whether advection or diffusion dominates transport: Pe = tA/tD = vl/Dj.

pe_fact_1.label: Neurospora Péclet Values
pe_fact_1.summary: In Neurospora growing at 1 μm s–1, Pe is ~0.3 for solutes (diffusion dominates) and ~20 for proteins (advection dominates) (Page 4).

mass_flow_evidence.label: Evidence for Mass Flow
mass_flow_evidence.summary: Use of oil droplets (non-interacting with motors) shows movement rates (~5 μm s–1) exceeding tip extension rates (0.2 to 0.5 μm s–1) (Page 4).

localization_scales.label: Localization Scales
localization_scales.summary: Scale of macromolecule localization depends on diffusion, advection, and degradation lifetime (τ).

loc_fact_1.label: Dimensionless Ratio C
loc_fact_1.summary: C = sqrt(Dj/v^2τ). If C > 1, diffusion dominates; if C < 1, flow dominates (Page 4).

water_economy.label: Water Economy and Permeability
water_economy.summary: The regulation of water uptake, movement, and loss to maintain turgor and enable mass flow.

membrane_permeability.label: Plasma Membrane Permeability
membrane_permeability.summary: The intrinsic resistance of the fungal membrane to water flow, influenced by lipid composition.

perm_fact_1.label: Yeast Permeability
perm_fact_1.summary: In yeast mutants lacking aquaporins, osmotic permeability (Pf) increases from 0.34 μm s–1 at 7°C to 2 μm s–1 at 23°C (Page 5).

ergosterol_fact.label: Role of Ergosterol
ergosterol_fact.summary: Presence of ergosterol (instead of cholesterol) is linked to greater resistance to desiccation (Page 5).

aquaporins.label: Aquaporins (AQPs)
aquaporins.summary: Specialized channel proteins that significantly increase membrane water permeability.

aqp_fact_1.label: AQP Impact
aqp_fact_1.summary: Overexpression of AQPs in yeast increases Pf by 9-fold at 7°C; Laccaria bicolor AQPs in Xenopus oocytes increase permeability up to 147 μm s–1 (Page 5).

water_loss_control.label: Control of Water Loss
water_loss_control.summary: Mechanisms to prevent evaporation and maintain internal hydration.

hydrophobins.label: Hydrophobins
hydrophobins.summary: Small (15 kDa) secreted cysteine-rich proteins that form a hydrophobic rodlet layer on aerial hyphae.

hydro_fact_1.label: Hydrophobin Function
hydro_fact_1.summary: They restrict water movement and evaporation autonomously based on water availability (Page 5).

matric_potential.label: Matric Potential
matric_potential.summary: Biophysical constraints on evaporation caused by cell wall pore diameter.

pore_fact_1.label: Pore Size in Achlya
pore_fact_1.summary: Experimental pore size in Achlya determined to be 2 nm, restricting evaporation even at low humidity (Page 6).

cellular_architecture.label: Cellular Architecture
cellular_architecture.summary: The structural organization of the hyphae, including septation and pore dynamics.

septation.label: Septation
septation.summary: The division of the apical cell into compartments via septa in Dikarya.

pore_types.label: Septal Pore Structures
pore_types.summary: Various pore types allowing cytoplasmic continuity.

pore_size_fact.label: Pore Dimensions
pore_size_fact.summary: Plasmodesmata: 10-70 nm; Other pore types: 50-500 nm (Page 6).

pore_occlusion.label: Pore Occlusion Mechanisms
pore_occlusion.summary: Structures that reversibly or irreversibly block septal pores.

occlusion_fact_1.label: Occluding Structures
occlusion_fact_1.summary: Woronin bodies (WBs) and SPA proteins in Ascomycetes; Septal Pore Caps (SPC) in Basidiomycetes (Page 6).

septal_dynamics.label: Fluid Flow through Septa
septal_dynamics.summary: The physics of cytoplasmic movement across septal constrictions.

flow_vel_fact.label: Septal Flow Velocity
flow_vel_fact.summary: Velocity (vp) is proportional to the relative area of the pore (rp^2/rh^2); measured in Neurospora in excess of 200 μm s–1 (Page 7).

wall_shear_stress.label: Wall Shear Stress
wall_shear_stress.summary: Mechanical forces produced by laminar fluid flow against the hyphal wall.

wss_formula.label: Shear Stress Formula
wss_formula.summary: τ = 4ηv/r, where η is dynamic viscosity, v is mean velocity, and r is vessel radius (Page 7).

wss_fact_1.label: Shear Stress at Septal Pores
wss_fact_1.summary: WSS at the septal pore is approximately (rh^3/rp^3) greater than elsewhere, producing forces large enough to degrade septa or trigger gene expression (Page 7).

growth_branching.label: Growth and Branching
growth_branching.summary: The mechanisms of hyphal extension and the creation of new tips.

branching_types.label: Branching Types
branching_types.summary: The spatial and regulatory modes of hyphal branching.

branch_fact_1.label: Branching Regulation
branch_fact_1.summary: Apical and subapical branching; daughter hyphae show negative autotropism regulated by the Cdc42 signaling pathway (Page 8).

growth_metrics.label: Growth and Volume Metrics
growth_metrics.summary: Mathematical relationships between volume, growth rate, and tip number.

growth_unit_fact.label: Hyphal Growth Unit
growth_unit_fact.summary: A constant volume of fungus per hyphal tip during exponential colony growth (Page 8).

nutrient_link.label: Nutrient-Growth Link
nutrient_link.summary: The dependency of growth and branching rates on substrate quality.

nutrient_fact_1.label: Vesicle-Branching Link
nutrient_fact_1.summary: Branching is more likely in regions with high density of tip-growth vesicles, often near septa (Page 9).

network_morphology.label: Network Morphology
network_morphology.summary: The macroscopic organization of the mycelium into different structural forms.

fusion_anastomosis.label: Fusion and Anastomosis
fusion_anastomosis.summary: The process of hyphal fusion to create loops and interconnected networks.

fusion_fact_1.label: Role of Loops
fusion_fact_1.summary: Loops improve network resilience and allow rapid reallocation of resources; essential for high rates of long-distance nutrient translocation (Page 10).

hyphal_aggregates.label: Hyphal Aggregates (Cords)
hyphal_aggregates.summary: Linear aggregates of hyphae used for long-distance transport.

cord_struct_fact.label: Cord Differentiation
cord_struct_fact.summary: Differentiation into thick-walled fiber hyphae and empty vessel hyphae (10-15 μm diameter) to improve flow (Page 10).

rhizo_struct_fact.label: Rhizomorph Anatomy
rhizo_struct_fact.summary: Consists of a central lacuna, inner medulla (large thin-walled vessel hyphae), outer medulla (2 μm wide hyphae), and a melanized hydrophobic rind (Page 11).

rhizo_cond_fact.label: Rhizomorph Conductivity
rhizo_cond_fact.summary: Longitudinal hydraulic conductivity (Lw||) varies from 1.5 to 3 x 10^-1 cm^2 bar^-1 s^-1 (Page 11).

quantitative_analysis.label: Quantitative Analysis
quantitative_analysis.summary: Mathematical and computational methods used to describe mycelial architecture.

fractal_geometry.label: Fractal Geometry
fractal_geometry.summary: Using fractal dimensions to quantify space-filling properties of mycelia.

fractal_dim_fact.label: Fractal Dimensions
fractal_dim_fact.summary: Mass fractal dimension (DM) and surface/border fractal dimension (DS). DM ranges from 1 (linear rhizomorphs) to close to 2 (dense mycelia) (Page 15).

box_counting_fact.label: Box-Counting Technique
box_counting_fact.summary: Method for calculating fractal dimension by overlaying grids of square boxes and counting intersections with the mycelium (Page 15).

graph_theory.label: Graph-Theoretic Representation
graph_theory.summary: Representing the mycelial network as a weighted, undirected graph.

graph_nodes_fact.label: Graph Nodes
graph_nodes_fact.summary: Nodes are located at hyphal tips, branches, and anastomoses (Page 17).

graph_weights_fact.label: Graph Edge Weights
graph_weights_fact.summary: Weights are based on cylindrical volume (V = πr^2L) for material cost or conductance (G = r^2/L) (Page 18).

centrality_fact.label: Betweenness Centrality
centrality_fact.summary: A measure of how important each cord is to transport through the network from the resource to every other node (Page 19).

computational_modeling.label: Computational Modeling
computational_modeling.summary: Theoretical models used to simulate fungal growth and resource translocation.

continuum_models.label: Continuum Models
continuum_models.summary: Models that represent the mycelium as a continuous density using differential equations.

continuum_fact_1.label: Reaction-Diffusion Stability
continuum_fact_1.summary: Morphological stability of colonies depends on nutrient and agar concentrations, explained by reaction-diffusion models accounting for waste inhibitors (Page 21).

agent_based_models.label: Spatially Explicit (Agent-Based) Models
agent_based_models.summary: Models that track individual hyphal tips as agents with specific behaviors.

abm_fact_1.label: Tip-and-Trail Modeling
abm_fact_1.summary: Hyphae are present wherever moving tips have passed; branching rates can be modeled as a function of internal resource concentration (Page 22).

add_model.label: ADD Model
add_model.summary: Advection-Diffusion-Delivery model used to predict resource translocation in complex networks (Page 11).

ecological_dynamics.label: Ecological Dynamics and Resilience
ecological_dynamics.summary: How mycelial networks interact with the environment and respond to damage.

foraging_strategies.label: Foraging Strategies
foraging_strategies.summary: Differing modes of space exploration and resource capture.

forage_fact_1.label: Phalanx vs. Guerrilla Foraging
forage_fact_1.summary: Phalanx foragers are slow-dense search fronts; Guerrilla foragers are fast-effuse, long-range systems (Page 13).

biomass_recycling.label: Biomass Recycling
biomass_recycling.summary: The degradation of redundant mycelial parts to redeploy resources to the growing margin.

recycle_fact_1.label: Recycling Mechanisms
recycle_fact_1.summary: Involves autophagy and controlled apoptotic-like mechanisms rather than necrosis (Page 12).

network_resilience.label: Network Robustness and Resilience
network_resilience.summary: The ability of the network to maintain function despite physical damage or grazing.

resilience_fact_1.label: Impact of Grazing
resilience_fact_1.summary: Collembola often graze on tips or fine hyphae; macrofauna like woodlice can sever thick cords. Resilience is increased by higher cross-connectivity (Page 23).

mycovirus_fact.label: Systemic Mycovirus Infection
mycovirus_fact.summary: Mycoviruses spread horizontally via hyphal anastomosis between compatible hosts; 30-80% of fungi harbor persistent infections (Page 24).

uncertainty_estimation.label: Uncertainty Estimation
uncertainty_estimation.summary: The process of quantifying the model's predictive reliability at each decoding step using multiple complementary metrics to capture different facets of confidence.

entropy_metric.label: Entropy
entropy_metric.summary: A measure of the dispersion of the probability distribution over the vocabulary, reflecting the concentration of the model's belief.

fact_entropy_formula.label: Entropy Calculation
fact_entropy_formula.summary: Calculated as the negative sum of (p_{t,c} * log p_{t,c}) divided by log |V|, where p_{t,c} is the probability of token c at step t and |V| is vocabulary size. Higher entropy indicates lower confidence. (Page 5)

least_confidence_metric.label: Least Confidence
least_confidence_metric.summary: An uncertainty measure based solely on the probability of the most likely (selected) token.

fact_lc_formula.label: Least Confidence Calculation
fact_lc_formula.summary: Calculated as 1 minus the probability of the chosen token p_{t,(1)}. Lower predicted probability corresponds to higher uncertainty. (Page 5)

margin_metric.label: Margin
margin_metric.summary: A measure of uncertainty derived from the difference between the top two token probabilities, capturing comparative distinctiveness.

fact_margin_formula.label: Margin Calculation
fact_margin_formula.summary: Calculated as the sigmoid of [1 - (p_{t,(1)} - p_{t,(2)}) / s], where s is a scaling factor. Smaller margins indicate greater ambiguity. (Page 5)

aggregated_uncertainty.label: Aggregated Token-Level Uncertainty
aggregated_uncertainty.summary: A unified uncertainty measure that combines entropy, margin, and least confidence using tunable weights.

fact_agg_formula.label: Aggregated Uncertainty Formula
fact_agg_formula.summary: u_{t,j} = w_{ent}u_{ent} + w_{mar}u_{mar} + w_{lc}u_{lc}. This integration captures distributional spread, decision confidence, and distinctiveness. (Page 5)

aggregation_mechanisms.label: Step and Trajectory Aggregation
aggregation_mechanisms.summary: Methods used to scale token-level uncertainty signals into rewards usable for reinforcement learning at the step and trajectory levels.

step_level_aggregation.label: Step-level Aggregation
step_level_aggregation.summary: The process of condensing token uncertainties within a single decision step into a single value.

fact_step_agg_formula.label: Step Aggregation Calculation
fact_step_agg_formula.summary: u_{step,t} is the average of token uncertainties u_{t,j} across the step. (Page 5)

trajectory_level_aggregation.label: Trajectory-level Aggregation
trajectory_level_aggregation.summary: The process of combining step-level uncertainties across an entire sequence of actions (trajectory).

fact_traj_agg_formula.label: Trajectory Aggregation Calculation
fact_traj_agg_formula.summary: Uses exponentially discounted aggregation: U(tau) = [Sum from t=1 to T of lambda^(T-t) * u_{step,t}] / [Sum from t=1 to T of lambda^(T-t)], where lambda is a discount factor prioritizing later steps. (Page 5)

reward_shaping.label: Failure-aware Reward Shaping
reward_shaping.summary: A mechanism that integrates uncertainty signals into rewards to ensure failed trajectories provide meaningful learning gradients rather than being discarded.

step_wise_shaping.label: Step-wise Shaping
step_wise_shaping.summary: Modifying the reward of individual steps based on failure status and normalized uncertainty.

fact_step_reward_formula.label: Step-wise Reward Formula
fact_step_reward_formula.summary: If fail: r_tilde = 1[fail] * w_t * u_{step_hat}. If success: r_tilde = r_t. w_t is typically set to 0.95 to ensure failure rewards are informative but lower than success rewards. (Page 5-6)

trajectory_level_shaping.label: Trajectory-level Shaping
trajectory_level_shaping.summary: Modifying the overall trajectory reward based on aggregated uncertainty in case of failure.

fact_traj_reward_formula.label: Trajectory Reward Formula
fact_traj_reward_formula.summary: If fail: r_tilde_traj = U(tau). If success: r_tilde_traj = r. (Page 6)

experimental_evaluation.label: Experimental Evaluation
experimental_evaluation.summary: Validation of SELAUR against baselines using interactive benchmarks to measure success rates and robustness.

benchmarks.label: Benchmarks
benchmarks.summary: Interactive environments used to test the agent's decision-making and generalization capabilities.

fact_alfworld.label: ALFWorld
fact_alfworld.summary: A benchmark emphasizing generalization in instruction following and compositional reasoning across household tasks. (Page 6)

fact_webshop.label: WebShop
fact_webshop.summary: A benchmark focusing on goal-oriented decision-making in realistic e-commerce environments, involving product selection. (Page 6)

baselines.label: RL Baselines
baselines.summary: Comparative reinforcement learning methods used to evaluate SELAUR's performance.

fact_ppo.label: PPO
fact_ppo.summary: Proximal Policy Optimization; competitive but less efficient due to the requirement of an extra critic network. (Page 7)

fact_rloo.label: RLOO
fact_rloo.summary: Reinforce-style optimization, computationally more efficient than PPO. (Page 7)

fact_grpo.label: GRPO
fact_grpo.summary: Group Relative Policy Optimization; provides balanced results and efficiency. (Page 7)

fact_gigpo.label: GiGPO
fact_gigpo.summary: Group-in-Group Policy Optimization; utilizes step-level reward modeling to improve fine-grained feedback. (Page 7)

ablation_studies.label: Ablation Studies
ablation_studies.summary: Tests conducted to determine the contribution of specific uncertainty metrics and reward formulations.

metric_synergy.label: Metric Synergy
metric_synergy.summary: Analysis of how different uncertainty measures complement each other.

fact_orthogonal_metrics.label: Metric Complementarity
fact_orthogonal_metrics.summary: Entropy captures overall distribution 'sharpness', while least confidence and margin focus on the competitive relationship between top actions. Full integration yields optimal performance. (Page 8)

reward_function_variants.label: Reward Function Variants
reward_function_variants.summary: Comparison of SELAUR's reward shaping against alternative uncertainty-based reward designs.

fact_negative_variant.label: Negative Reward Variant
fact_negative_variant.summary: Replaces failure rewards with negative values to penalize uncertainty; underperforms by limiting exploration in uncertain states. (Page 8-9)

fact_exponential_variant.label: Exponential Reward Variant
fact_exponential_variant.summary: Attenuates success rewards by exp(-u_step); underperforms because excessive discounting weakens the reinforcement of successful behaviors. (Page 8-9)
